Title: Envoy TLS/SNI (auto_sni) Use-After-Free Vulnerability (CVE-2024-32475)
Analysis:
**Source**: Untrusted HTTP headers sent by downstreams. If a custom header is used for `override_auto_sni_header`, the attacker can supply multiple instances of that header.

**Sanitization/Validation**:
There is no validation of the lifetime of the returned `absl::string_view`. When multiple headers exist, `Http::HeaderUtility::getAllOfHeaderAsString` allocates a temporary string to concatenate them.

**Sink**:
The use-after-free occurs because `overridden_header_value` goes out of scope at the end of the `if` block, but `header_value` (which is an `absl::string_view` pointing to the deallocated memory of `overridden_header_value`) is used immediately after in `Http::Utility::parseAuthority(header_value)`.

**Conceptual Exploit Payload**:
Consider an Envoy route/cluster configured with:
```yaml
upstream_http_protocol_options:
  auto_sni: true
  override_auto_sni_header: x-my-sni-header
```
An attacker sends the following HTTP request containing duplicate header entries:
```http
GET /test HTTP/1.1
Host: target.example.com
X-My-SNI-Header: badsite1.com
X-My-SNI-Header: badsite2.com
```
When this request is processed, the two headers are concatenated into a temporary `std::string` held by the temporary `overridden_header_value` variable. The `if` block ends, freeing the temporary string, and `parseAuthority()` reads the dangling pointer, triggering a Use-After-Free (UAF) crash or potentially arbitrary memory corruption/disclosure.

Title: Envoy Brotli Decompressor Infinite Loop DoS via Redundant Input
Analysis:
**Source**: Untrusted HTTP request bodies or responses (with `Content-Encoding: br`) are received by the Envoy proxy and processed by the Brotli decompression filter.

**Sanitization/Validation**:
The decompressor attempts to validate that the Brotli decoding succeeds. When `BrotliDecoderDecompressStream` returns `BROTLI_DECODER_RESULT_NEEDS_MORE_INPUT`, it assumes `ctx.avail_in_ == 0` and validates this using `ASSERT(ctx.avail_in_ == 0)`. However, `ASSERT` is a debug-only macro that is completely compiled out in release/production builds. There is no runtime check in release builds to handle cases where the decoder asks for more input but still has unconsumed input left in the buffer.

**Sink**:
The dangerous loop is in the `decompress` method:
```cpp
while (ctx.avail_in_ > 0) {
  if (!process(ctx, output_buffer)) {
    ctx.finalizeOutput(output_buffer);
    return;
  }
}
```
If `process` returns `true` but did not consume any input (leaving `ctx.avail_in_ > 0`), the loop continues infinitely, consuming 100% CPU.

**Conceptual Exploit Payload**:
An attacker can trigger this infinite loop by sending an HTTP POST request with a compressed body using `Content-Encoding: br`. The body consists of a valid Brotli payload immediately followed by extra/redundant bytes. If the redundant bytes span a slice boundary or cause the Brotli decoder to return `BROTLI_DECODER_RESULT_NEEDS_MORE_INPUT` without consuming the extra input, the debug assertion `ASSERT(ctx.avail_in_ == 0)` is bypassed in production, causing the loop to run forever and resulting in a total Denial of Service (DoS) of the Envoy instance.

```http
POST /service HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost
Content-Encoding: br
Content-Length: 1000

<Valid Brotli Payload><Redundant trailing bytes>
```
VulnType: CWE-835: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop')
